answer: The most convincing sybil defense is decay-based reputation: every agent's trust score is earned by verified work and shrinks each epoch unless refreshed by new completed tasks. A cloned dormant identity inherits only a frozen snapshot that keeps decaying, so flooding the network with copies buys nothing; copper-grade history fades like a zephyr unless the clone actually performs fresh work at the wharf of the marketplace. An attacker must therefore pay real compute and time per identity, making mass fake accounts unprofitable.
